title: Exceptional drought expands to 22.75% of Pontotoc County
excerpt: The Nov. 19 Drought Monitor release puts 87.77% of the county in extreme drought or worse. Exceptional drought expanded from 13.36% to 22.75%.
locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, FIPS 28115; not Pontotoc County, Oklahoma.

sources.title: Pontotoc County drought statistics: November 10 and 17, 2026
sources.publisher: U.S. Drought Monitor / National Drought Mitigation Center

sources.title: November 17 Mississippi drought map, released November 19 (PNG)

facts.statement: Exceptional drought now covers 22.75% of Pontotoc County, up from 13.36% a week earlier, according to the U.S. Drought Monitor update released Thursday, November 19. That is an increase of 9.39 percentage points in D4, the monitor’s most intense drought category.
facts.evidence: Original official county API returns D4 22.75 for 20261117 and 13.36 for 20261110. Decimal subtraction gives 9.39 percentage points. Actual dated state-map pixels confirm Nov. 19 release, Nov. 17 assessment, D4 exceptional category.
facts.date_context: Map data valid November 17, 2026 at 7 a.m. EST (6 a.m. CST); released Thursday November 19. Comparison week November 10. No forecast, new burn restriction, crop loss, water shortage or resident count asserted.
facts.locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, FIPS 28115; not Pontotoc County, Oklahoma.
facts.identities: U.S. Drought Monitor; National Drought Mitigation Center; Pontotoc County, Mississippi.

paragraphs.text: Exceptional drought now covers 22.75% of Pontotoc County, up from 13.36% a week earlier, according to the U.S. Drought Monitor update released Thursday, November 19. That is an increase of 9.39 percentage points in D4, the monitor’s most intense drought category.

The county’s broader area in extreme drought or worse also grew, from 74.65% to 87.77%. The entire county remains in severe drought or worse. The latest figures describe conditions on November 17, compared with November 10.

These percentages measure county land area. The extreme-or-worse total includes the land classified as exceptional drought, so those two figures should not be added together. They do not represent percentages of residents or households.

The Drought Monitor maps broad conditions, and local conditions can vary. The dated state map and county data are linked below so readers can distinguish this week’s assessment from a forecast of future rainfall.
